recipes.name: Koji tomahawk
recipes.sub: Thirty-day dry-aged flavor in two days. Koji enzymes build the umami and the crust sugar; the smoker and one violent sear do the rest.
recipes.label: FIRE
recipes.blurb: 2 to 3 day age · cook-day clock · reverse sear
ingredients: tomahawk, 2 inch plus (minimum 1.5 inches for any cut; trim silverskin first, enzymes cannot get through it)
plain unsalted dried rice koji (blitzed coarse in a spice grinder, not to flour)
compound: tallow, garlic, shallot, rosemary (plus the saved koji crust; for basting and the board)
kosher salt and flaky salt (a touch lighter than a normal steak; clean crunch to finish, never iodized)

recipes.name: Grilled pork chops
recipes.sub: Soy and brown sugar marinade, two-zone fire, peach and tomato relish from whatever the market had. The last cook wrote its own rules; they are in here.
recipes.label: FIRE
recipes.blurb: marinade · two-zone fire · peach relish
ingredients: ripe peach (half diced for relish, half halved for the grill)
red onion (half minced for relish, rest in thick skewered rings)
zucchini or yellow squash (planked lengthwise, 1/2 inch)

recipes.name: Bacon-wrapped hot dogs
recipes.sub: The toothpick spiral is a myth. The vendor method cooks the bacon flat first and lets the rendered fat glue the seam shut.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: vendor method · seam sealed in fat
ingredients: thin-cut bacon (thin conforms and bonds; thick fights you)
mayo, mustard, ketchup, grilled onions and peppers, jalapenos

recipes.name: Chashu pork belly
recipes.sub: Texas smoker, carnitas-style braise, Japanese chashu roll. Two days: the braise, then the overnight seal, then slice and pack. Captain’s own build, still being pinned down.
recipes.label: FIRE
recipes.blurb: smoker braised · two days · black gold
ingredients: and more (the rest of the rub has not been named yet)
whatever else the cabinet offers on the day

recipes.name: Peruvian-style grilled chicken
recipes.sub: Boneless, skinless thighs in a soy, lime, cumin and smoked paprika marinade, grilled hot and fast over the coals, 6 minutes a side, off at 175°F and rested. A mild green herb sauce in the aji verde style, a big salad on the house vinaigrette, rice for the boys. Set the time you want to eat and everything runs itself backward.
recipes.label: FIRE
recipes.blurb: two-zone grill · mild green sauce · big salad
ingredients: cilantro, packed (leaves and tender stems, about 1 bunch at 4 servings)
cherry tomatoes (halved; a pint is about 2 cups)
jasmine rice (water to the rice cooker's line)

recipes.name: Shrimp scampi
recipes.sub: Thirty minutes from water on, and the last fifteen are hands-on. Frozen shrimp need thawing before any of that, and the clock covers it. Set the time you want to eat and everything runs itself backward.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: 30 min · linguine, wine, lemon
ingredients: large shrimp (peeled and deveined, tails off)
unsalted butter (half to sear, half to finish)

recipes.name: Carbonara
recipes.sub: Restaurant-silky Roman carbonara. The blender dissolves the cheese into the eggs before heat ever touches them, so the sauce cannot go gritty.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: 25 min · blender emulsion · mayo method inside
ingredients: guanciale, rind trimmed (family swap: thick center-cut bacon, least sweet and smoky, no maple)
Pecorino Romano, finely grated (too sharp for the family: go 3 parts pecorino, 1 part Parmigiano)
salt for the pasta water (about 5 g per liter; the pork and cheese carry the rest)

recipes.name: Sausage and antipasto pasta
recipes.sub: Mild sausage, blistered artichokes and roasted red peppers, capers, and a sauce that physically cannot break. The pot that became a house method.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: aioli method · make-ahead sauce
ingredients: mild Italian sausage (mild: you cannot spice the boys out of dinner)
olive oil (to reach 3/4 cup total fat at the 4-serving build)
grated parm (75 to 90 g at the 4-serving build)
caper brine (the acid; nothing foreign added)
black pepper (no salt in the aioli; the parm and sausage carry it)

recipes.name: Baked bacon mac and cheese
recipes.sub: Velveeta does the stability, block cheese does the flavor. Built the night before; the clock below runs the reheat.
recipes.label: OVEN
recipes.blurb: make-ahead · reheat clock · serves 8
ingredients: Velveeta, cubed (a US block is 907 g; the 8-serving build uses less than half)
sharp cheddar, block, grated (block only; pre-shredded has coatings that will not melt right)
smoked paprika (plus a pinch for the topping)

recipes.name: Meatballs
recipes.sub: Beef and pork, one egg per pound, panade soaked to paste. The oven does the rest.
recipes.label: OVEN
recipes.blurb: beef and pork · 400F · by the pound

recipes.name: Kentucky hot brown
recipes.sub: The Brown Hotel's 1926 original. Open-faced turkey on toast, smothered in Mornay, broiled bubbling, crossed with bacon. Derby day royalty.
recipes.label: OVEN
recipes.blurb: Derby day · Mornay · broiled
ingredients: kosher salt, black pepper, fresh nutmeg
roasted turkey breast, sliced thick (deli counter off the bone, sliced thick, is a fine shortcut)

recipes.name: Mortadella sandwich
recipes.sub: Bourdain's five-ingredient sandwich from Appetites, off the one at Bar do Mane in Sao Paulo. Fried, not dried.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: Bourdain · fried, not dried
ingredients: mortadella (ask the deli to slice it thin so it crisps)

recipes.name: Pot roast
recipes.sub: Classic pot roast, scaled by the weight of meat you have. A hard sear, the aromatics and a red wine deglaze in the cast iron, then the Instant Pot for the rest: pressure in homemade chicken stock and wine, the gravy thickened, the carrots and rutabaga 3 minutes under pressure in it, the meat back in big chunks and everything on Slow Cook until dinner. A garlic and rosemary Yukon Gold mash on the same clock, ready with it.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: scales by meat weight · cast iron sear · Instant Pot · slow cook finish
ingredients: boneless chuck roast (the weight you have drives the page; best as two pieces, well marbled)
yellow onions (in thick wedges; don't skimp)
head of garlic (cloves peeled and smashed)
carrots (in 1.5 inch chunks; in for the 3 minute finish)
rutabaga (in 1 inch chunks; in with the carrots)
beef tallow (for the sear in the cast iron)
black pepper, freshly ground (after the sear)
Yukon Gold potatoes (matched to the meat, 1 to 1)
garlic and rosemary (for the mash butter)

recipes.name: Taco Thursday chicken tacos
recipes.sub: Chicken thighs, dry brined since Tuesday, pressure cooked in salsa verde with onion, garlic, lime, oregano and one whole chipotle for smoke. Store run at 3:30, pot on at 4:15, and it holds on Keep Warm while you fetch the kids. At 6:00 the chicken is shredded into its juices, broiled for crisp edges, and the tortillas are charred on the burner. Mild for the boys, heat on the side for you. Set the time you want to eat and everything runs itself backward.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Instant Pot pressure cook in salsa verde · broiled crisp · charred tortillas · heat on the side
recipes.time: about 3 hours from the store run
ingredients: boneless skinless chicken thighs (already salted and dry brined, so no more salt)
salsa verde (one 16 oz jar at 4 servings)
chipotle in adobo (whole, from the tin, for smoke not heat; it comes out before serving)
white onion, for the pot (peeled and halved)
lime, juiced into the pot (about 2 tbsp juice per lime)

recipes.name: Cajun red beans and rice
recipes.sub: Stage one, under 30 minutes the night before: the beans get a quick soak in the Instant Pot while the sausage and the trinity brown in cast iron, then it all goes into the Instant Pot insert and the fridge. Stage two, the morning of: stock and Cajun seasoning in, a 30 minute hard boil for safety, then Slow Cook before you leave. Home at 5:00, rice in the rice cooker, dinner at 6:30. For a Wednesday dinner that is Tuesday 9:00 pm and Wednesday 6:03 am. Mild for the boys, hot sauce on the side. Set the time you want to eat and every step, the night-before ones included, runs itself backward, each with its day and date.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Night before: quick soak and cast iron brown · morning: 30 minute hard boil, then slow cook all day · rice at 5
ingredients: dried red kidney beans (sorted, any stones or shrivelled beans out)
hot tap water, for the quick soak (hot water comes to pressure sooner; it goes down the sink after)
chicken stock (enough to cover the beans by about 1 inch; top up with water if not)
white rice (dry, measured with a standard cup)
water, for the rice (or to the rice cooker's white rice line)
hot sauce (on the table for the grown-ups only)
kosher salt, in the pot (the sausage brings salt too; sized for Diamond Crystal; Morton is about twice as salty, use half)
kosher salt, at the finish (up to this much, after tasting; sized for Diamond Crystal; Morton is about twice as salty, use half)
kosher salt, for the rice (sized for Diamond Crystal; Morton is about twice as salty, use half)
sweet paprika (this and the next seven make the mild Cajun seasoning)
cayenne (the only heat in the pot, kept mild for the boys)

recipes.name: Grillades and grits
recipes.sub: Sunday, Louisiana week, tonight's dinner only. Active time: about 2 hours, from 4:26 for 6:30, with no real hands-off stretch. The roux is the long pole: a fat-heavy roux takes about 70 minutes to reach copper at 325 to 345°F and wants a stir every minute or two, and the medallions, the sear, the Instant Pot and the grits fit around it. With a jar of copper roux already in the fridge it drops to about 1 hour. A beef chuck tender roast sliced across the grain into medallions and pounded thin, seared hard in the cast iron, pressure cooked with its juices, beef stock and tomatoes, then married into a copper roux gravy with the trinity, over cheddar grits. Half the roux goes into a pint jar for Monday's gumbo at no extra work.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: Cast iron sear · Instant Pot braise · copper roux gravy · cheddar grits · active about 2 hours

recipes.name: Chicken and andouille gumbo
recipes.sub: About 40 minutes at lunch, then it simmers all afternoon. Monday, Louisiana week, home all day: one pot, the Dutch oven, built from 12:30 to about 1:10, then a bare simmer on the lowest setting until dinner at 6:30, with a stir about every hour. Andouille and chicken thighs browned in the pot, Sunday's jar of copper roux darkened in their fat, the trinity, the homemade broth. Rice into the rice cooker at 5:45.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: One pot · built at lunch from 12:30 · simmers all afternoon · Sunday's jar of copper roux

recipes.name: Rotisserie chicken broth
recipes.sub: Instant Pot, pressure cooked. Frozen rotisserie chicken carcasses go straight in with the spare onion, celery, a bay leaf and cold water to the PC MAX line, then Pressure Cook High 90 minutes and a natural release. Strained into an ice bath, into jars and the fridge. Set the time you start and every step counts forward from it: a 2:47 start strains about 5:10 and is in the fridge by 6:20. The come-up and release times are estimates.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Instant Pot · frozen carcasses · High 90 · natural release · strained about 5:10
recipes.time: start 2:47 pm, strained about 5:10, in the fridge by 6:20

recipes.name: Rice cooker rice
recipes.sub: Plain rice in the rice cooker, for under a sauce or a gumbo. Washed, water to the line, start. The cooker takes 45 minutes and then holds the rice on Keep Warm. Active time: about 6 minutes at an easy pace. From a 6:00 start the rice is ready at 6:51.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Rice cooker · washed, water to the line · 45 minutes

recipes.name: Fried grit cakes with andouille Creole sauce
recipes.sub: Thursday, Louisiana week. The andouille Creole sauce simmers in the Instant Pot on Slow Cook all day, and one pan of Sunday's leftover cheese grits is fried crisp in the cast iron when you walk in. Active time: about 20 minutes at the counter the night before, 2 minutes in the morning, then about 20 minutes of easy work between 6:00 and 6:30. Nothing happens at the stove before 6:00.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Sauce slow cooked all day in the Instant Pot · one pan of Sunday's grits fried crisp · 20 minutes from 6:00
recipes.time: pot on at 6:50 am, cakes from 6:00, eat at 6:30
ingredients: piece of Sunday's leftover cheese grits

recipes.name: Fried grit cakes
recipes.sub: Leftover cheese grits, cut cold, dusted with flour and fried crisp in the cast iron in beef tallow at 375°F, 5 minutes a side. One pan, six pieces. Active time: about 18 minutes at an easy pace, 30 minutes from pan on to plate. The cheese grits have to be made ahead and set cold in the fridge.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: Leftover cheese grits · cast iron · 5 minutes a side at 375°F

needs.hint: Uses leftover cheese grits, set cold in the fridge. None left over?

recipes.name: Dirty rice
recipes.sub: Thursday, Louisiana week. Active time: about 40 minutes: 3 at 5:16 to start the rice cooker (it takes 45 minutes), then 35 from 5:55 to 6:30. Ground pork, ground beef or breakfast sausage browned hard in the cast iron with tonight's trinity, diced fresh, garlic and Cajun spice, then tonight's rice, steamed dry on a sheet pan, fried through it with a splash of stock and soy. Frozen green beans steamed on the side. The ground meat thaws in the fridge the night before.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: Tonight's rice · ground meat and trinity · about 40 minutes active
ingredients: ground pork, ground beef or breakfast sausage

recipes.name: Carne guisada
recipes.sub: Monday night, Instant Pot. One chuck pot roast in 1.5 inch cubes, seared hard in the cast iron, onion and bell pepper in the drippings with garlic, chili powder, cumin and oregano, then 25 minutes under pressure in tomato and beef stock, gravy thickened with a flour slurry at the end. Rice and tortillas. Mild in the pot, jalapeno on the side. Set the time you want to eat and every step runs itself backward.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Cast iron sear · Instant Pot 25 minutes · slurry gravy · rice at 5:10

recipes.name: Slow cooker tom kha
recipes.sub: Her recipe: the 40 Aprons Slow Cooker Tom Kha Soup. Onion, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, lime leaves and red curry paste steep in chicken stock on High for 3 hours, the aromatics come out, then coconut milk, chicken and mushrooms go in for about an hour more. Sugar, fish sauce and lime to finish. In the Instant Pot on Slow Cook. Mild for the boys over rice; the chile and chili oil are on the side for him.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: her recipe, 40 Aprons · Instant Pot slow cook · mild, heat on the side
ingredients: stalk lemongrass (cut in 3 inch lengths and bruised)
red Thai curry paste (can be halved if the boys find it warm)
chicken stock (made up from chicken stock powder: 1 tsp powder to each cup of hot water)
red jalapeno (or 1 to 2 Thai chiles; sliced, out of the pot)
jasmine rice (water to the rice cooker's line)

recipes.name: Cast iron pork chops, onion and pear pan sauce
recipes.sub: Bone-in chops seared hard in cast iron after the onions have gone slowly golden in the same pan with butter. Pears in with the onions, the fond lifted with apple cider, a knob of butter to finish, over the house mash on the burner next door. Fresh off the heat at 6:30. Set the time you want to eat and everything runs itself backward.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: cast iron · onion and pear cider pan sauce · house mash
ingredients: large yellow onion (halved and sliced thin)
apple cider (the drink, not the vinegar)
chicken stock (made up from chicken stock powder: 1 tsp powder to each cup of hot water)
kosher salt, for the potato water
kosher salt, for the mash (taste, then up to half as much again)
Parmesan, finely grated (at home; not too much)

recipes.name: Peppercorn mushroom sauce
recipes.sub: A pan sauce built on brandy, cream and cracked pepper, made in the steak pan. The house cut runs the mushrooms fine so they melt in like a duxelles.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: steak pan sauce · brandy and cream
ingredients: mushrooms, finely diced (or 12 oz, sliced, for the chunky version)
black peppercorns, coarsely cracked (cracked, never ground; the backbone)
green peppercorns in brine, drained (optional; the steakhouse pop)

recipes.name: Andouille Creole sauce
recipes.sub: Andouille, the trinity, tomatoes and Cajun seasoning, slow cooked all day in the Instant Pot. The insert is loaded the night before, the pot goes on in the morning, and at dinner the sauce is waiting on Keep Warm for whatever it goes over: fried grit cakes, rice, cheese grits, potatoes. Active time: about 20 minutes at the counter the night before, 2 minutes in the morning, and about 8 minutes of easy work at dinner. Nothing happens at the stove.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Slow cooked all day in the Instant Pot · over grit cakes, rice or cheese grits
recipes.time: pot on at 6:50 am, ready at dinner

recipes.name: Bacon-fat aioli
recipes.sub: The house master technique. A mayonnaise built from rendered fat and egg cannot break or scramble on hot food. No thermometer, no tempering.
recipes.label: JAR
recipes.blurb: master ratio · cannot break
ingredients: total fat, warm to the touch (rendered bacon or sausage fat, topped up with olive or neutral oil)
acid or water (lemon, caper brine, jar liquid, whatever the dish gives)
finely grated hard cheese (if the dish wants it; 1.5x everything for a pound of pasta)

recipes.name: Base vinaigrette
recipes.sub: The standing house dressing, built straight in the salad bowl. The Dijon emulsifies; the olive brine seasons without more salt.
recipes.label: JAR
recipes.blurb: olive brine · built in the bowl
ingredients: olive oil (working ratio, to be locked on a book cook)

recipes.name: Wilted house salad
recipes.sub: Chopped olive, romaine and tomato on the base vinaigrette, wilted on purpose. Closer to a marinated salad than a tossed one.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: wilted on purpose · romaine
ingredients: romaine (the go-to; chopped iceberg holds too. Spring mix turns to mush)

recipes.name: Steamed green beans
recipes.sub: Frozen green beans steamed from frozen in a small saucepan for 7 minutes, then tossed in butter. No trimming. Active time: about 5 minutes at an easy pace, 15 minutes from water on to the table.
recipes.label: PAN
recipes.blurb: Frozen green beans · steamed from frozen, 7 minutes · butter

recipes.name: Mashed potatoes
recipes.sub: Yukon Golds boiled in salted water and riced, folded with half a stick of butter and a little good olive oil that have slowly confited garlic and fried rosemary, stopped with a cup of cream, loosened with their own cooking water, finished with salt, MSG and a little Parmesan. Two burners at once. Scaled by the weight of potatoes.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: garlic confit butter · riced · two burners · his own process
ingredients: Yukon Gold potatoes (peeled, in 1.5 inch chunks)
kosher salt (for the water and the mash)
bay leaf (optional, if you're feeling fancy)
unsalted butter (half a stick at 3 lb)
extra virgin olive oil (2 tbsp at 3 lb)

recipes.name: Cheese grits
recipes.sub: Grits cooked in water with powdered chicken stock, finished with butter and sharp cheddar. About 40 minutes at an easy pace: about 10 for the water to boil, then 25 on low with a stir every 5 minutes. Active time: about 15 minutes. From a 6:00 start they are ready at 6:40. What is left sets firm in the fridge for fried grit cakes.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Water and powdered chicken stock · butter and sharp cheddar · sets firm for grit cakes

ahead.txt: 3 minutes. Spread what is not being eaten tonight about 3/4 inch deep in a dish. Once it stops steaming, cover it and into the fridge. It sets firm overnight and keeps three to four days.

recipes.name: Quick pickles
recipes.sub: The all-purpose brine, everything by weight so it scales without thinking. Cucumbers, onions, jalapenos, carrots, most anything.
recipes.label: JAR
recipes.blurb: 1:1 brine · 10% sugar · 3% salt
ingredients: white vinegar, 5% acidity (the house batch ran 350 g; it all scales)
kosher salt, non-iodized (iodized clouds the brine)

recipes.name: Pickled carrots and cabbage
recipes.sub: The quick-pickle brine pointed at carrots and cabbage. The carrots outlast the cabbage; both outlast the week you meant to eat them in.
recipes.label: JAR
recipes.blurb: house brine · months in the fridge
ingredients: quick-pickle brine (see Quick pickles for the weights)

recipes.name: Pickled eggs
recipes.sub: The keeper version. Soy-marinated eggs are a five-day item; a vinegar brine buys you weeks.
recipes.label: JAR
recipes.blurb: vinegar brine · the keeper version
ingredients: quick-pickle brine (see Quick pickles; mostly vinegar is what preserves)

recipes.name: Mint julep kit
recipes.sub: Heat kills mint. The cold blend ruptures the leaves without it: an intensely green, aggressively minty syrup, tested and ratioed.
recipes.label: CUP
recipes.blurb: cold-blend syrup · tested ratios
ingredients: fresh mint leaves, stems off (garden mint cut the same day wins; the oils fade in hours)
cold water (the blender needs this much liquid to pull a vortex; learned the hard way)

recipes.name: Watermelon rum punch
recipes.sub: Milk-clarified, crystal clear, pours like a spirit. Plan two days and never squeeze the curds.
recipes.label: CUP
recipes.blurb: milk-clarified · 2 days · keeps a month
ingredients: fresh watermelon juice (about 8 lb cubed flesh, strained hard)

recipes.name: Cold brew, Cafe du Monde
recipes.sub: The chicory blend runs hot: fine grind, fast extraction. Shorter steep than the internet tells you.
recipes.label: CUP
recipes.blurb: 80 g per quart · 12 to 14 hr
ingredients: Cafe du Monde grounds (fine grind, chicory-heavy)
cold water (what actually fits with the insert in a quart jar)

recipes.name: Movie-theater popcorn
recipes.sub: Two routes to the real thing: the Flavacol build that IS theater popcorn, and the tallow version that started it.
recipes.label: POT
recipes.blurb: Flavacol or tallow · salt the oil
ingredients: coconut oil (what the chains actually use)
Flavacol (Gold Medal's fine yellow theater salt; one carton lasts years)
ghee (closest real-food stand-in for theater topping; melted butter's water makes it soggy)
salt plus a tiny pinch of sugar (salt first sticks to the shell; the sugar is the theater sweetness)

recipes.name: Smoked ribs
recipes.sub: Test kitchen: being dialed in. What the record holds so far, nothing invented.
recipes.label: TEST
recipes.blurb: modified 3-2-1 · being dialed in

recipes.name: Smoked chicken thighs
recipes.sub: Test kitchen: being dialed in. What the record holds so far, nothing invented.
recipes.label: TEST
recipes.blurb: 250F · being dialed in

recipes.name: BBQ sauce
recipes.sub: Test kitchen: exists, undocumented. The build lives in the Captain's head.
recipes.label: TEST
recipes.blurb: undocumented · first sauce day writes it
